The Productivity Boom Central Banks Can’t See

Central banks are fighting the last war. Their models treat strong growth as overheating. That rule was built in a decade of 1 per cent productivity growth, and it is about to break.

Fed and Wall St currently want rate hikes into a disappearing Energy Supply shock. While ignore the productivity boom standing right in front of them! 

Artificial intelligence is now speeding up its own development. 

The old growth is Bad mantra needs to be abandoned!

At Anthropic, code shipped per engineer is more than 45 times the 2024 rate. 

Combined revenue at the leading AI labs is growing more than fourfold a year. AI capital spending is about $ 1 trillion, roughly the size of the US defence budget. 

The next step is AI agents doing white-collar work, and white-collar wages total about $ 30 trillion worldwide.

That is a supply shock, and supply shocks lower prices. Look at the compute market. Rental prices for small blocks of GPUs are falling as new capacity floods in. Prices are rising only for very large training clusters, where power and interconnection are the bottleneck. 

Research shows that where supply can respond, prices fall. Inflation survives only where there is a hard physical constraint, and it is temporary.

The macro data agree. US productivity is up 16 per cent since 2019, and unit labour costs fell in the third quarter. Strip out shelter and US core CPI is 2.0 per cent. What remains is energy, a supply shock already reversing.

The risk is policy error. Raising rates into a productivity boom chokes the investment that creates the supply. Growth is not the enemy of price stability. In this cycle, growth is the cure.

There is this particular guy I met in Glasgow. A jolly fellow who always spoke up for the "oppressed."

We have been chatting online for quite a while and he seemed like a very decent individual.

I have no idea what his government name is, cos I only know him by his IG username.

2 days in Glasgow, I linked up with him, had a few talks, strolled around and ended up at my porch.

We had a full indepth talk about everything we believed in, and thats when I realized how hollow he is. (SMH).

We talked about the lore behind his push for money, and all he said was he needed to make money so he can have "power."

I was disappointed, but I knew where he was driving to, so i kept indulging him.

He said there are a lot of things he can't do in Scotland. He can't host parties and block parts of the road, he can't get a team of policemen to escort him around the area, he can't pay his was into getting a van of Soldiers, escorting him out.

He said he has people who have "offended" him and he wants to show them he has arrived (I don't know what that means).

He said he has already bought and shipped over 8 vehicles to his house in Nigeria, and he can't wait to go home for the Yuletide and make noise with it all, without anyone reporting him for noise pollution.

Finally, I asked him who he would vote for, if he were to participate in the January election... He said Tinubu, because everything he dreams of, can only be possible if he is in power.

Anyways, I've blocked him... Thank God we didn't share contacts, so our only line of communication is gone... Only mistake I made was inviting him to my space, and that can also be restrained, all thanks to the working judiciary.

Leopold Aschenbrenner says he spends half his day with "finance-folk who think AI is over" and the other half with SF people who think the models will do their jobs within a year. 

His new Situational Awareness letter makes clear which side he's on. These are the important numbers:

- AI is now speeding up AI research. Algorithmic progress is running 2-3x faster, overall progress 1.5-2x. At Anthropic, agents log 19 hours of work for every hour a human researcher works, and code shipped per engineer is up more than 45x since 2024.

-METR estimates Anthropic is improving its models about twice as fast as before, ~80% of that thanks to AI. And remember, Anthropic itself says in its S-1 update it may soon hit its own RSP threshold (>2x acceleration from AI).

- The forecast for 2027: a median of 3 years of AI progress in a single year! That's another GPT-4 to Opus 5.5 jump on top of today's models. From 2028 comes "physical RSI": AI designs the chips (OpenAI's Jalapeño went to tapeout in 9 months) and robots build the data centers.

- Next paradigm: "virtual departments". Hundreds to thousands of agents running for weeks under manager agents. OpenAI's 10,000-agent swarm on Navier-Stokes was an early version.

The curves are bending upward. RSI has started.

UBS — a Swiss bank — now projects Chinese-made AI chips will hold 88% of China's own market by 2028 📈

Shipments: 1.7M units in 2025 → 10M+ by 2030

Read that twice. Western finance is now the loudest voice announcing that Western containment failed

Washington accidentally built Beijing's best sales team, and Wall Street is just here to put a bullish price target on the wreckage 

The trajectory: China's domestic share was 14% in 2023. 41% in 2025. 64% in H1 2026. Huawei sits at 28%, six points behind Nvidia — a gap three years of sanctions and one CEO scandal have nearly closed

UBS's front-runners? Cambricon Technologies and Biren Technology — not because their silicon dazzles anyone, but because they locked up fab capacity and cloud partnerships. In 2026 the moat isn't architecture. It's allocation

And credit where due — Washington has been generous. First it banned the chips. Then it banned the workarounds, welding shut the third-country data centers that carried 46% of Chinese AI compute. Then it set Jensen Huang's USD 11B-a-quarter China comeback on fire as a parting gift. Moonshot tore up a $150M contract via Indonesia before Washington could even finish the paperwork

Nothing accelerates import substitution like being told you can't import

But buried in the fine print: UBS still expects supply to run 20–30% short of demand through 2028 — and 88% of cards shipped is not 88% of compute. Domestic accelerators still trail flagship Nvidia silicon on per-chip performance, so you need more of them to do the same work

Second, and more importantly, the real moat moved from silicon to software. Winning 88% of shipments when your main competitor is legally barred from selling isn't winning the ecosystem. CUDA is the actual wall — and four domestic software stacks are busy reinventing it four times at once

Huawei is open-sourcing CANN, putting CNY 5 billion behind ecosystem development over the next three years, opening 10k-NPU-scale compute to the community, and working directly with labs like DeepSeek — whose joint supernode work already has 128 Ascend 950s running real training workloads. Until the market converges on one standard — most likely Huawei's — Chinese engineers are stuck optimizing across incompatible hardware

And finally, the whole projection leans on SMIC turning sanctions-era DUV into a 10-million-unit miracle

But the direction is set. Washington spent a decade guarding a door China was already walking through — then handed over the whole market on the way out. The Empire doesn't just lose markets anymore. It delivers them 🫡
